governed_construct: Each function or method definition (def / async def, at any nesting level) and each class definition in the file. Lambdas are not instances.
interpretation: The rule requires every function, method and class to carry a docstring (a string literal as the first statement of its body) written in Google style. A class conforms if it has a docstring. A function conforms if (a) it has a docstring; (b) when it declares any parameters other than a leading self/cls (including *args and **kwargs), the docstring has an 'Args:' section line and each such parameter appears in it as an entry 'name:' or 'name (type):' (with leading * or ** for variadics); (c) when its own body (excluding nested defs) contains a 'return <expr>' whose value is not a bare None, the docstring has a 'Returns:' section; (d) when its own body contains yield, the docstring has a 'Yields:' section ('Returns:' not required). A 'Raises:' section is allowed but not required. A function with no documentable parameters and no returned value conforms with a summary-only docstring. Sphinx/reST style (':param x:', ':returns:') and NumPy style ('Parameters' / '----------' underlines) do not conform, because they lack the Google 'Args:'/'Returns:' sections. A missing docstring on any instance, an undocumented parameter, or a missing Returns/Yields section makes the whole file VIOLATED. Files with no def or class are NOT_APPLICABLE. Content of strings and comments that merely look like definitions are not instances.
